supporting_observations.claim: At 13:44:43 UTC, PowerShell ran on WS-DREYES-01 as paul.becker with the command line for the inventoried Patch-Workstations.ps1 script.
A remote logon for paul.becker was recorded on WS-DREYES-01 shortly before the PowerShell execution, and that logon received special privileges.
The PowerShell process launched wusa.exe to install a Windows 11 update package, and both processes subsequently exited.

The logged PowerShell activity is consistent with the organization’s documented workstation-patching practice and is a plausible explanation for the reported brief window, though its recorded start is several minutes after the approximate reported time.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records do not establish what Dan Reyes saw on screen or identify the exact time of the reported brief window.
The PowerShell record is at 13:44:43 UTC, not around 13:40 UTC; the available evidence does not link a specific window displayed at 13:40 to that process.
The records show the script path and command line, but not the script contents.
claims_not_established: Whether a separate, unlogged PowerShell window appeared around 13:40 UTC.
Whether the reported window was the later workstation-patching PowerShell process.
Whether the script performed only the actions indicated by its name and the observed update installation.
unrelated_findings: Google Drive File Stream is not among the approved storage services in the provided inventory; a Google Drive process and related proxy activity were recorded on WS-DREYES-01. Review separately; this does not determine the disposition of the reported PowerShell activity. (T124-00143, T124-00402, T124-00404)
